articleBody:
- [ ] Exterior threshold flashing check — Confirms flashing directs water away from bottom jambs and stops water intrusion before trim is set.
- [ ] Framing plumb and square measurements — Identifies bowed studs around garage doors so your contractor can shim casing evenly.
- [ ] Clearance measurement above concrete floor — Ensures baseboard and door casing stay slightly elevated above the slab to prevent moisture wicking.
- [ ] Material specification review — Confirms solid paint-grade wood or moisture-tolerant composite is selected instead of moisture-sensitive interior MDF.
- [ ] Back-priming verification on raw wood cuts — Verifies that hidden faces and cut end grain receive primer to stop humidity absorption behind walls.
- [ ] Wall finish readiness confirmation — Drywall finishing and initial wall priming should be fully completed before casing installation begins.
- [ ] Fastener schedule into solid framing — Verifies casing nails drive straight into wall studs rather than gripping only drywall core.
- [ ] Cure time for wood fillers — Ensures nail hole fillers dry for the recommended curing window before finish sanding starts.

How to use this checklist:
Review these concrete checkpoints with your finish contractor during your initial walkthrough. Addressing framing flaws, drainage, and correct materials before trim boards are cut prevents warped moldings and premature rot.
